skill.name: karpathy-llm-wiki
skill.description: Use when building or maintaining a personal LLM-powered knowledge base. Triggers: ingesting sources into a wiki, querying wiki knowledge, linting wiki quality, 'add to wiki', 'what do I know about', or any mention of 'LLM wiki' or 'Karpathy wiki'.
skill.summary: Build a source-grounded Markdown wiki with ingestion, cited answers, explicit archives, and evidence checks.
skill.author: astro-han

security_audit.summary: All 105 static findings are false positives after contextual review of the flagged files. Matches reflect Markdown formatting, project-relative links, inert test data, temporary test directories, and a local subprocess call without shell execution. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or data exfiltration in the reviewed files.

content.user_title: Build and Maintain a Source-Grounded LLM Wiki
content.value_statement: Scattered sources make personal knowledge difficult to retrieve and verify. This skill organizes preserved sources into linked Markdown articles with cited answers and evidence checks.
actual_capabilities: Preserve collected source text with metadata under raw, then classify ingestion as New, Update, Disputed, or No material.
Create or merge topic articles with source citations, conflict annotations, related links, index entries, and operation logs.
Search the index and full wiki text to answer questions with article citations without writing files during ordinary queries.
Archive answers as new, explicitly requested snapshot pages with links to cited wiki articles.
Run a read-only Python checker for selected numbers, dates, longer quotations, evidence-link errors, and unreferenced raw files.
Apply specified index and link repairs during lint while reporting factual problems for review.
limitations: Source retrieval depends on the host environment providing web or file tools; inaccessible sources require pasted content.
Mechanical evidence checks cover selected literal forms, not every fact, source credibility, or semantic entailment.
The evidence checker requires Python 3.10 or later and reports issues without fixing files.
Wiki articles support one topic directory level; archived answers are snapshots and do not receive cascade updates.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Literature Wiki
use_cases.description: Ingest papers and notes, connect recurring concepts, and mark disagreements while preserving the original source text.

use_cases.title: Track Technical Decisions
use_cases.description: Compile technical sources into topic articles, compare options through cited queries, and archive requested decision summaries.

use_cases.title: Keep Reference Notes Verifiable
use_cases.description: Organize reference material and review unsupported quotations, stale claims, broken links, and uncompiled sources before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Add a First Source
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [source URL or pasted text] to my wiki under [topic]. Preserve the source text and report the ingestion disposition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: initialize the knowledge base through a first ingest.

prompt_templates.title: Ask a Cited Question
prompt_templates.prompt: What does my wiki say about [topic]? Search the index and article text, cite relevant articles, and do not write files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: retrieve existing knowledge without changing the wiki.

prompt_templates.title: Review Wiki Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Lint my wiki at [project root]. Apply only documented safe fixes, run evidence checks, and report factual issues without rewriting claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: maintain index, links, and source fidelity.

prompt_templates.title: Research and Archive a Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] from supporting and opposing perspectives. Ingest sources sequentially, annotate conflicts, then archive a cited comparison as a new page.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: explicitly authorize multi-source research and an archived synthesis.

output_examples.input: Add a source that introduces a new concept and challenges an existing article.
output: Preserved the source text with collection and publication metadata.
Created a concept article and marked the conflicting claims in the related article.
Updated the index and appended an ingest log entry.

output_examples.input: What does my wiki say about the tradeoffs between two approaches?
output: The cited articles support different approaches under different operating constraints.
One article emphasizes implementation simplicity; the other emphasizes maintenance cost.
The answer links to the relevant wiki articles and distinguishes unresolved disagreements.

output_examples.input: Lint a wiki with an unsupported statistic, a broken evidence link, and an unused source.
output: Fidelity suspect: an article statistic was not found verbatim in its linked raw sources.
Evidence error: a Raw link could not be resolved.
Inventory reminder: a raw source has no article reference or No material log entry.
Factual issues remain unchanged pending review.

best_practices: Locate exact numbers, dates, and quotations in linked raw sources before adding them to an article.
Compile sources one at a time so shared index, log, and cascade updates remain consistent.
Review evidence suspects against their source context and preserve disagreements through explicit status annotations.
anti_patterns: Do not rewrite preserved raw sources or silently replace historical claims.
Do not treat a clean literal-matching report as proof that every statement is accurate.
Do not launch research or save ordinary query answers without explicit user authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It organizes preserved sources under raw and compiled Markdown articles under wiki, with an index and append-only operation log.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for all three tools. Available file, web, and command tools determine which workflow steps can run.

faq.question: Does asking a question change my wiki?
faq.answer: Ordinary queries return cited answers without writing files. Saving an answer requires an explicit archive request.

faq.question: Does the evidence checker verify every fact?
faq.answer: No. It checks selected numbers, ISO dates, and longer quotations against linked raw text. Other claims require contextual review.

faq.question: What happens when a source adds nothing new?
faq.answer: The source is preserved and logged as No material. The workflow stops without forcing a new article.

faq.question: Will archived answers stay current automatically?
faq.answer: No. Archives are point-in-time snapshots. Lint can report archives whose cited articles changed substantially, but cascade updates do not rewrite them.
